findings.reason: §2 is dispatched first on its own write paths and would land without the constant, so §8's readiness read names an object nothing defines.
findings.text: §8 says `RUN_DELIVERED_STATUSES` in `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py` is a constant "which §2 introduced", but §2 (snapshot line 47-49) never specifies it and names no such symbol in its mechanism, so the predecessor node has nothing telling the implementer to create it

findings.reason: without an arm that mutates the queued pointer's brief the node cannot show its guard fires; a discriminating arm leaves `steering.md` alone and changes the pointer's stored `node.brief`, or edits `steering.md` directly and requires the launched digest to follow it.
findings.text: §5's negative arm ("edits the original `--brief` source file after dispatch, and the worker reads the text as dispatched") passes on the unfixed code, because `dispatch()` already copies the brief into the run directory at dispatch (`reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1816` calls `_store_brief` there), so the arm cannot distinguish a launch-time read of `steering.md` from today's dispatch-time copy

findings.reason: the only test of the delivered set measures acceptance rather than delivery, so the node's gate can be green while a failed upstream launches its tail; it needs an arm where an upstream closes `blocked` or `failed` and the waiter moves to `blocked-upstream`.
findings.text: §8's assertion that "every status the delivered set names is one `parse_manifest` accepts" holds by construction once the set is derived from `TERMINAL_MANIFEST_STATUSES`, and it would pass on the very derivation defect that finding `reasoning` names

findings.reason: a worker fenced to the stated paths cannot implement `--after` and must stop for a scope extension, which is the cost §2 and §5 avoid by naming their CLI module; it also omits the `--after` option itself from the mechanism's description of what is new.
findings.text: §8 introduces `--after <request-id>` for a brief dispatch but declares write paths only for `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py`, `reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py` and a new test file, while the option must be parsed and carried by the dispatch command surface (the module that registers `crew dispatch`, alongside the `TaskNode` it builds)

findings.reason: it inverts the DAG guarantee the section exists to provide; the repair is to derive delivered from a delivered-status set (a `completed`-only member of the vocabulary, or a small named set §8 owns).
findings.text: §8 says "the delivered set is derived from `TERMINAL_MANIFEST_STATUSES` in `reckon/crew/reports.py`, not restated", but that set is `{"complete", "blocked", "failed"}` (`reports.py:126`), so deriving it makes a failed or blocked upstream count as delivered and lets the waiter launch, while §2 (line 47) requires a ref closed as abandoned or failed to move its dependents to `blocked-upstream`
